title: Feather on Jazz compilations and Freddy Steps Out
summary: Barnet says Universal let Leonard Feather re-edit shorts, and agrees Freddy Steps Out was a weak musical.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: "Feather on Jazz," originally produced by MCA-TV, a series of jazz programs, and there's just about everybody listed here. There's Charlie Barnet in "Melody Parade." That's probably incorporating one of your other pictures.
It seems to me that Will Cowan told me that Universal made a deal with Leonard to take a bunch of these shorts and re-arrange them or something and put them out.

I saw part of something, it must have been part of this, that he showed in a class he was teaching, and he like cut out all of the non-band material. He'd cut out the dancers and the novelty acts and things and put it together.

That's probably what that is . Okay. 672 is "Freddy Steps Out," 1946, 63 minutes, directed by Arthur Dreifuss, listed as a second rate musical comedy without very much of either, featuring Charlie Barnet.
